commentary.text: I’m claiming a central square immediately with Red, creating the first anchor for a center-occupation win while keeping multiple Red pieces available as future sandwich endpoints.
I’m taking a central square beside Red’s advanced piece, establishing pressure while keeping the remaining Blue edge pieces available as supporting flanks.

Yellow takes the lower-left center. Blue’s piece beside Red is now vulnerable to a Red sandwich from the right, and any Green piece entering the adjacent lower-right center would face the same pattern from Yellow.
I’m developing Green toward the open central square while blocking Yellow’s direct route up column 4. This also keeps the piece clear of an immediate sandwich.
Red closes the horizontal sandwich around Blue’s central intruder. This removes a Blue piece, advances its loss count, and clears the upper-right center for Team A.
I’m contesting the center immediately. Yellow can potentially sandwich this Blue piece, but doing so costs tempo and opens the central square for Green to occupy safely on the following turn.

Yellow mirrors Red’s tactic, landing to the right of Blue and using the Yellow center anchor as the far flank. This takes a second Blue piece and restores both lower center squares to Team A or emptiness.
I’m occupying the open upper-center square, safely stepping between the two Red pieces. This blocks Team A’s immediate center-occupation plan while preserving Green’s central mobility.

Red advances above Green to restrict its central mobility and build a vertical flanking structure. The move also keeps the existing Red anchors intact while increasing control around the last contested center square.
Blue advances toward the center, preparing to occupy (4,4) while supporting Green’s existing central foothold.

Yellow fills the lower-right center, sealing Green’s central piece on all four sides. Green cannot move that piece now, while Team A occupies three of the four center squares and can work on a triggered capture of the final blocker.
I’m exploiting the existing Green flank on (3,4): landing on (3,2) sandwiches and captures the Red center piece, weakening Red while opening a central square for Team B.

Green broke the original Red anchor, so Red shifts beside the vacancy to prepare a replacement. From here Red threatens to drop onto (3,3), which would use the surviving Red at (3,5) to sandwich the Green center blocker.
I’m withdrawing the exposed Blue piece before Yellow can sandwich it via (6,4). On (5,3), it stays close to the center while avoiding an immediate capture.

Yellow places a flank to the left of Blue’s exposed piece on row 5. With Yellow still at (4,4), the next threat is to land on (5,4) and sandwich Blue against this new endpoint, forcing Blue to spend its next turn escaping or lose its third piece.
I’m consolidating Green’s central foothold while keeping both pieces protected and contesting the opponent’s two occupied center squares.

Green’s move aligned both central Green pieces between an open landing square and Red’s surviving flank at (3,5). Red now drops onto (3,2), capturing both Greens in one sandwich and bringing Green to two losses.
I’m shifting the exposed Blue piece out of Yellow’s immediate sandwich threat while establishing a far flank against Yellow’s central piece on (4,4).

Blue escaped the horizontal trap but stepped directly between Yellow’s center piece and the open square below. Yellow lands at (6,4), completes the vertical sandwich, and takes Blue’s third loss to eliminate the color.
I’m advancing Green toward the open central square at (3,4), while avoiding the immediate sandwich traps around Yellow’s formation on row 4.

With Blue eliminated and unable to capture, Red occupies the upper-right center. Team A now holds three central squares, and the Red piece at (3,2) is poised to fill the remaining square; Green has no immediate route to occupy that vacancy.
I’m shifting a Void Blue piece inward to constrain the central file and prepare it as a durable team blocker near Green’s advanced piece.

Yellow preserves both occupied lower-center squares and develops an outside piece without opening any capture against the center formation. Red’s winning entry into the remaining center square stays ready for the next turn.
I’m advancing Green beside the central Yellow pair, creating a potential same-color sandwich across row 4 while contesting the crowded center.
Red steps into the last vacant central square. Together with Red at (3,4) and Yellow on both lower center squares, this completes Team A’s four-square center occupation and wins immediately.
